turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, good morning. I have brought my son Arjun, he is six. He has fever and cough, kindly see him.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good morning. Sorry, one second, this screen has frozen again. Fever and cough — since when?
[SEG0003] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): From three days, doctor. It started Sunday night. Before that he was completely fine.
[SEG0004] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Three? No, it is five days. From Friday itself he was warm in the evening. I am his grandmother, I stay in the house and look after him in the daytime, so I know.
[SEG0005] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): On Friday he went to school and he ate well. It is three days only. I mean — not four, three.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Say that again, please? I was typing and I missed it. Three days or five?
[SEG0007] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Five days the fever is there. I checked with the thermometer, it was one hundred and three.
[SEG0008] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It was one hundred and one on our digital thermometer, doctor, not one hundred and three.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll just put a few days for now, you can sort the number later. Arjun, does your tummy hurt?
[SEG0010] person_4 (PATIENT): No, sir.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Has he vomited?
[SEG0012] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting, doctor.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any rash, or loose motions?
[SEG0014] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Nothing like that. He is passing urine as usual.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Arjun, is the cough worse at night?
[SEG0016] person_4 (PATIENT): I ate idli and sambar this morning, sir.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hmm, the screen jumped. I was asking about the cough in the night, not about breakfast.
[SEG0018] person_4 (PATIENT): The idli was very nice, sir.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, I'll leave it. Is the cough more at night?
[SEG0020] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, doctor. Night time it is more. He is waking up two times, sometimes three.
[SEG0021] person_3 (CAREGIVER): In the day also he is dull, not playing. He is not taking food properly, only a little rice.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fast breathing? Chest going in?
[SEG0023] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Breathing is normal, only the cough is there.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): What have you given him?
[SEG0025] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Crocin syrup by mouth, for the fever. One small teaspoon, three times a day, from yesterday.

[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It was not a small spoon. She gave two big kitchen spoons, I saw it. And last night I gave Ibugesic syrup by mouth, maybe half a spoon, only one time, because of the fever. I did not measure it properly.
[SEG0027] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ibugesic? I did not know you gave that. And my Crocin was one small spoon, not two. I am sure.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the computer beeped. Say the Ibugesic again.
[SEG0029] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Ibugesic syrup, maybe half a spoon, once, last night only. For the fever.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines?
[SEG0031] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, doctor. No allergies.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any asthma, or any old problem?
[SEG0033] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No asthma. Last year they did a haemoglobin blood test, and the paediatrician said it was borderline. He never told us the number.
[SEG0034] person_4 (PATIENT): They said it was borderline, sir.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): When last year, which month?
[SEG0036] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I don't remember the month. Sometime last year only. We did not repeat it.
[SEG0037] person_3 (CAREGIVER): In December also he had a cold. It went away by itself in four days, so we didn't come then. The traffic today was very bad, that is why we are a bit late, sorry.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fine. Arjun, please open your mouth and sit still.
[SEG0039] person_4 (PATIENT): Yes, sir.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): The throat is red. Chest has no wheeze, air entry is good both sides, no indrawing. Ears look fine.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Vitals on this screen — temperature 38.4 degrees, pulse 124, oxygen 98 percent, respiratory rate 26. It keeps flickering, but those are the numbers.
[SEG0042] person_4 (PATIENT): Sir, my stomach is hurting a little.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your stomach? You said no a minute ago. Where does it hurt?
[SEG0044] person_4 (PATIENT): In the middle, sir. Only a little.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): I was going to send a chest X-ray and start an antibiotic syrup.
[SEG0046] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He is drinking water well, doctor. And that December cold settled without antibiotic.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Chest is clear and the oxygen is good, so I am changing the plan. No X-ray today, and no antibiotic.
[SEG0048] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Then what will you do, doctor?

[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): A complete blood count today, instead, to see the infection picture. And a proper paracetamol dose. This looks like a viral fever with cough. I cannot rule out a mild bacterial infection until the blood count is back, but I am not calling it pneumonia.
[SEG0050] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The blood test today itself?

[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. I will order the complete blood count now, at the lab downstairs, before you leave. Paracetamol suspension, two hundred and fifty milligrams in five ml — give five ml by mouth, four times a day, after food. Stop the Ibugesic completely.
[SEG0052] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Five ml, four times, and stop Ibugesic. I will write it down.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): Use the measuring cup, not the kitchen spoon. Give plenty of fluids, light food, and sponge him if he is very hot.
[SEG0054] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He is in class one, he already missed two days. There is a small rhyme programme, but tell us about school first.

[SEG0055] person_2 (DOCTOR): No school until he has been fever-free for one full day. Come back in three days for review. Come sooner if he becomes very dull, stops drinking, or starts breathing fast.
[SEG0056] person_4 (PATIENT): Thank you, sir.
[SEG0057] person_3 (CAREGIVER): We will go to the lab now. Thank you, doctor.

features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats
